title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Management Measures on Strictly Regulating the Entrustment of Enforcement Matters (Trial)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Measures for the Management of Strictly Regulating the Entrustment of Enforcement Matters (Trial Implementation)"

Fa Fa [2017] No. 27

To: All High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Measures for the Management of Strictly Regulating the Entrustment of Enforcement Matters (Trial Implementation) of the Supreme People's Court are hereby issued to you for diligent implementation.

September 8, 2017

Measures for the Management of Strictly Regulating the Entrustment of Enforcement Matters (Trial Implementation)

To strictly regulate the entrustment of enforcement matters by the people's courts, strengthen mutual assistance and cooperation among courts in different regions, leverage the functional advantages of the enforcement command center, save human and material resources, and improve work efficiency, these Measures are formulated in light of the actual circumstances of the enforcement work of the people's courts.

Article 1 Where a people's court encounters any of the following matters that require handling in a different locality during the enforcement of a case, it may entrust the relevant local court to handle the matter on its behalf:

(1) Freezing, renewing a freeze, unfreezing, or deducting bank deposits or wealth management products;
(2) Publicly freezing, renewing a public freeze, or unfreezing equity interests or other investment rights and interests;
(3) Sealing up, renewing a seizure, unsealing, or transferring title to immovable property and movable property requiring registration;
(4) Investigating the property status of the person subject to enforcement;
(5) Other matters specified in the enforcement matters entrustment system of the people's courts.

Article 2 Where the entrustment involves investigating the property status of the person subject to enforcement, the entrusting court shall specify in the entrustment letter the specific content of the investigation, the specific entity assisting with the enforcement, and attach the corresponding notice of assistance in enforcement. The subject matter of the investigation shall be property types and scopes not yet supported by the central-to-central ("total-to-total") asset inquiry and control system.

Article 3 All entrustments of enforcement matters by the entrusting court shall be initiated and processed through the enforcement case handling system, and shall not be conducted by mailing physical materials offline. Where the entrusted court receives physical materials mailed offline, it shall contact the entrusting court to submit the entrustment of matters online before proceeding to handle the matter.

Article 4 When initiating an entrustment of enforcement matters, the handling judge of the entrusting court shall, in the matters entrustment module of the case handling system, enter the name of the entrusting court, the name of the entrusted court, the case number, the entrusted matter, the processing deadline, the name and contact information of the handling judge, and attach the relevant legal documents. After approval, the entrustment of matters shall be pushed to the Enforcement Matters Entrustment System of the People's Courts. The enforcement command center of the entrusting court shall verify the documents, affix an electronic seal, and push the matter to the entrusted court.

Article 5 The entrusted court shall generally be the basic people's court at the location where the entrusted matter is to be handled, unless entrusting a court at the same level is more conducive to the handling of the entrusted matter.

Article 6 The processing deadline shall be reasonably estimated based on the specific matter, generally not less than ten days and not exceeding twenty days. Where urgent handling is required, after pushing the entrustment of the matter, the entrusting court shall contact the entrusted court through the enforcement command center, and the entrusted court shall complete the handling within 24 hours.

Article 7 The relevant legal documents shall include the enforcement ruling, the notice of assistance in enforcement, the letter of entrustment for enforcement, and the service certificate (or receipt), and shall be accompanied by scanned copies of the enforcement official's identification. Where the entrustment involves deducting frozen funds, scanned copies of the enforcement basis shall be provided and affixed with the electronic seal of the entrusting court.

Article 8 Upon receiving an entrustment of enforcement matters through the Enforcement Matters Entrustment System of the People's Courts, the entrusted court shall verify the materials as soon as possible, accept the entrustment, and proceed with handling.

Article 9 Where the entrusted matter falls outside the scope listed in Article 1 of these Measures and the entrusted court cannot handle it, the entrusted court may, after communicating with the entrusting court, return the matter.

Article 10 Where the legal documents provided by the entrusting court do not meet the requirements or lack necessary documents, and the entrusted court cannot handle the matter, it shall promptly communicate with the entrusting court to inform it of the materials that need to be supplemented. Without such communication, the entrusted court shall not directly return the entrustment. The entrusting court shall supplement the materials through the system within three days; if the matter still cannot be handled after supplementation, the entrusted court may return the matter after stating the reasons.

Article 11 The entrusted court shall promptly accept and handle the entrustment of enforcement matters. After completion, it shall promptly feedback the handling status, service certificate, receipt, or other materials to the entrusting court through the system. The entrusting court shall promptly confirm the closure of the matter.

Article 12 The entrustment of enforcement matters shall not be filed as an entrusted enforcement case. The entrusted court shall, based on its local actual conditions, convert the entrusted matters into enforcement implementation cases at a certain ratio, count them towards the workload of enforcement personnel, and include them in the scope of performance assessment.

Article 13 The entrusting court may, in the Enforcement Matters Entrustment System of the People's Courts, evaluate completed entrustments, or file a complaint with the higher court of the entrusted court, stating the specific reasons for the complaint. The complained entrusted court may explain the circumstances through the matters entrustment system. Evaluation and complaint information shall serve as an indicator for assessing the work regarding entrusted matters.

Article 14 Each High People's Court and Intermediate People's Court shall diligently fulfill its supervisory duties, and through the Enforcement Command Management Platform, supervise courts under its jurisdiction regarding untimely acceptance and handling of matters, and untimely confirmation of case closure. The Supreme People's Court and High People's Courts shall periodically compile statistics on and circulate notices regarding the handling of entrusted matters by courts under their jurisdiction.
